title: Move only P1 epoch-ticket allocation off the W/X launch prologue
mechanism: For the existing selected z/x P1 instances, move the even-word atomicAdd ticket allocation from the prologue to immediately before its first epoch/acquire wait. Keep the zeroer, odd-word release publication, acquire poll, bounded trap, reduction, S and grid unchanged. On a single ordered CUDA stream each completed launch still consumes exactly S tickets/tile and one flag increment; prove this rather than reset counters.
why_current: Actual scored router8 is x/S16, router16 z/S16, router32 z/S8; unpooler1/8 use x/S4. The matched PW38 router8 SASS has ticket ATOMG at0x350 before X/W LDG0x410/0x460 and later acquire waits. Static PC order is not timing proof; this is a placement experiment, not an atomic-count reduction.
cpu_discriminator: State-machine proof for arbitrary CTA arrival order and repeated graph launches, source-bound physical alias/counter transitions, then one new compile-time placement bit at fixed selected geometries. Explicitly model unsupported concurrent-state streams and hold them rather than assume one epoch.
falsifier: Ticket issue already overlaps all useful work, moving it delays the final acquire critical path, any epoch/alias test fails, or paired complete-kernel delta loses. Old midstream flag-prefetch no-gain evidence is not counted as support.
new_proof: Exact per-launch counter deltas and zero-before-reduction ordering must remain identical. No speculative output, removed acquire, extra graph node or host-maintained replay epoch.
